minutes.headline: Conservation Commission approved the Hickory Hills lake drawdown plan and, over two no votes, the Leominster Shirley Road gravel site plan.
minutes.summary: Several routine hearings were continued to January 2nd. The commission approved the Hickory Hills drawdown plan with conditions. After long debate it approved the gravel site berm plan, with two members opposed. It also raised a daily fine, declined to pursue a Chapter 61 first refusal, and continued the online filing surcharge discussion. Members aired disagreement over the gravel site vote at the end.

public_comment.topic: A Hickory Hills representative presented the lake drawdown plan and supporting data.

votes.motion: Continue the Kilburn Street notice of intent to January 2nd
Continue the 51 Fire Road notice of intent to January 2nd
Approve the Hickory Hills drawdown notice of intent with conditions (stream flow method by spring, annual approval of depths, winter measurements as safety allows)
Approve the gravel site plan as presented, with the 20-foot strip and no-stockpile area shown on the plan
votes.outcome: passed; two members voted no, Richard birch's vote unclear

votes.motion: Increase the fine at 101 Pleasant Street to three hundred dollars per day
Ratify the enforcement orders for 131 and 133 Leominster Shirley Road
Draft a letter supporting the open space plan
Send a letter to the Board of Selectmen not recommending the right of first refusal at 994 Northfield Road
Approve certificate of compliance for 554 Lancaster

Send an enforcement order to Shady Point about beach erosion

budget_items.topic: Online permitting surcharge on conservation fees
budget_items.what_was_said: A surcharge on filing fees would help pay for the town's online permitting software. Members debated whether it should apply to all fees and whether taxpayers subsidise permits.

budget_items.topic: Cost of appraisals for a Chapter 61 first refusal
budget_items.what_was_said: Exercising the town's right requires two certified appraisals, and the town has no money for them.

decisions.decision: The online filing surcharge discussion was continued while the agent consults the town's permitting contact.
The agent will tell the Emerald Place beach owners that a fine will be voted if there is no action by January 2nd.
The order of conditions for the lake management matter will go on the January 2nd agenda.
Bob Pease will raise with the open space committee a process to flag Chapter 61 parcels early and a rollback tax fund.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission approved the gravel site berm plan on Leominster Shirley Road with the 20-foot strip and no-stockpile area; two members voted no.
The commission approved the Hickory Hills lake drawdown plan with conditions on stream flow method, annual approval of depths and winter measurements.
The commission raised the daily fine at 101 Pleasant Street.
A letter to the Board of Selectmen not recommending the right of first refusal at 994 Northfield Road was moved; the vote was not audible, and appraisal costs were noted as unfunded.
The online filing surcharge discussion was continued while the agent consults the town's permitting contact, and an enforcement order on Shady Point beach erosion passed.

why_it_matters: The gravel site approval and the lake drawdown conditions set what happens near a river and a lake, and the plans' conditions are what the town can enforce later.
If the town cannot pay for two appraisals, it may be unable to use its right of first refusal on Chapter 61 land, so such land may leave protected status without a town bid.
A surcharge on conservation filing fees would shift part of the cost of online permitting software onto applicants, and the commission has not yet decided whether it applies to all fees.
watch_next: January 2nd: continued hearings at Kilburn Street and 51 Fire Road, the lake management order of conditions, and the Emerald Place beach deadline for a possible fine.
The agent's consultation with the town's permitting contact on the online filing surcharge.
